en: Keep the receipt safe, you will need it for returns.
tamil: ரசீதை பத்திரமா வச்சுக்கோங்க, திருப்பிக் கொடுக்க அது வேணும்.
context: Advice from a salesperson after you buy.
explain: 'Keep' plus an adjective means to stay in that state. 'Will need' says what is necessary later.

en: Can I return this if it does not fit?
tamil: பொருந்தலன்னா இதை திருப்பிக் கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking about the return rule before buying.
explain: 'If it does not fit' is a condition. 'Return' here means to give a product back.

en: You can exchange it within seven days.
tamil: ஏழு நாளுக்குள்ள மாத்திக்கலாம்.
context: Explaining the shop's exchange policy.
explain: 'Can' shows that something is allowed. 'Within seven days' means before seven days are over.

en: I want a refund, the screen is cracked.
tamil: எனக்கு பணம் திரும்ப வேணும், திரை விரிசல் விழுந்திருக்கு.
context: Complaining about a damaged product.
explain: A refund is money given back. Giving the reason after a comma makes your request clear.

en: I ordered this phone online last Sunday.
tamil: இந்த போனை போன ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை ஆன்லைன்ல ஆர்டர் பண்ணேன்.
context: Telling when you placed an order.
explain: 'Ordered' is past tense. 'Last Sunday' tells the time in the past.

en: When will my order be delivered?
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் எப்போ டெலிவரி ஆகும்?
context: Asking customer care about delivery time.
explain: 'Will be delivered' is the future passive. We use it when the action matters more than who does it.

en: The delivery boy has not come yet.
tamil: டெலிவரி பையன் இன்னும் வரல.
context: Telling someone a parcel is still pending.
explain: 'Has not come yet' is present perfect negative. 'Yet' shows we are still waiting.

en: They sent me the wrong size again!
tamil: அவங்க திரும்பவும் தப்பான சைஸ் அனுப்பிட்டாங்க!
context: Being annoyed about a wrong delivery.
explain: 'Sent' is the past of 'send'. 'Again' shows this has happened before.

en: Is cash on delivery available in my area?
tamil: என் ஏரியால கேஷ் ஆன் டெலிவரி இருக்கா?
context: Checking payment options before ordering.
explain: 'Cash on delivery' means you pay when the parcel arrives. 'Available' means you can get it.

en: I am checking the reviews before I buy it.
tamil: வாங்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி ரிவ்யூ பாத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Explaining careful online shopping.
explain: 'Am checking' shows an action happening now. 'Before I buy' tells what comes after.

en: Have you tracked your parcel on the app?
tamil: ஆப்ல உன் பார்சலை ட்ராக் பண்ணியா?
context: Asking a friend about their delivery.
explain: Present perfect asks about an action with a result now. 'Tracked' is the past participle of 'track'.

en: Never buy anything from a link that looks suspicious.
tamil: சந்தேகமா தெரியுற லிங்க்ல இருந்து எதையும் வாங்காதீங்க.
context: Giving online safety advice.
explain: 'Never' plus a base verb is a strong warning. 'Suspicious' means it looks unsafe.

en: The shop gives a one-year warranty on the fridge.
tamil: கடை ஃப்ரிட்ஜுக்கு ஒரு வருஷ உத்தரவாதம் தருது.
context: Describing what comes with an appliance.
explain: A warranty is a promise to repair a product for some time. 'One-year' joins a number and a noun with a hyphen.

en: We are going to buy a new washing machine this weekend.
tamil: இந்த வார இறுதியில புது வாஷிங் மெஷின் வாங்கப் போறோம்.
context: Sharing a shopping plan.
explain: 'Going to' shows a plan you have already made. 'This weekend' is the near future.

en: Do you accept credit cards or only cash?
tamil: கிரெடிட் கார்டு எடுத்துக்குவீங்களா, இல்ல கேஷ் மட்டும்தானா?
context: Asking about payment methods at a small shop.
explain: 'Or' joins two choices in a question. 'Accept' means to agree to take something.

en: I don't have change for a five hundred rupee note.
tamil: என்கிட்ட ஐநூறு ரூபாய் நோட்டுக்கு சில்லறை இல்ல.
context: Telling the shopkeeper you only have a big note.
explain: Here 'change' means small coins and notes. 'Don't have' is the simple negative for owning something.

en: She bought a silk saree for the festival last week.
tamil: அவ போன வாரம் பண்டிகைக்கு பட்டுப் புடவை வாங்கினா.
context: Talking about festival shopping.
explain: 'Bought' is the past of 'buy'. 'For the festival' tells the purpose.

en: Which offer is better, buy one get one or twenty percent off?
tamil: எந்த ஆஃபர் நல்லது, ஒண்ணு வாங்கினா ஒண்ணு இலவசமா, இல்ல இருபது சதவீத தள்ளுபடியா?
context: Comparing two shop offers.
explain: 'Which' is used when choosing between a few options. 'Better' compares two things.

en: Everything here is fixed price, sir.
tamil: இங்க எல்லாமே ஒரே விலைதான், சார்.
context: A seller explaining that bargaining is not allowed.
explain: 'Fixed price' means the price does not change. 'Sir' is a polite way to speak to a customer.

en: I could not find parking, so I walked to the market.
tamil: பார்க்கிங் கிடைக்கல, அதனால சந்தைக்கு நடந்து போனேன்.
context: Explaining how you reached the market.
explain: 'Could not' is the past form of 'cannot'. 'So' joins a reason and a result.

en: My budget is only two thousand for the whole month.
tamil: என் பட்ஜெட் ஒரு மாசம் முழுக்க இரண்டாயிரம்தான்.
context: Explaining a limit on spending.
explain: 'Only' shows that the amount is small. 'The whole month' means from start to end.
